key_insight: BISECT improves continual learning by splitting low-rank updates into shared and novel feature directions rather than treating all cross-task overlap as interference.
engineering_relevance: The approach could support sequential adaptation of vision-based engineering inspection models, though solid-mechanics applications are not evaluated in the abstract.
method: Partition a fixed LoRA rank budget into dominant joint historical–current modes and an orthogonal novelty complement.
Extract novelty directions using generalized Rayleigh whitening followed by orthogonal complement projection.
Merge trained updates into the frozen backbone, gating shared rank-1 atoms by current-to-joint Rayleigh ratios and preserving novelty atoms at unit gain.
evidence_signal: Across eight incremental settings on five vision datasets, BISECT reportedly outperforms prompt, adapter, and LoRA baselines without extra inference parameters or FLOPs; historical null tails capture only 5.5% of incoming-task variance.
watch_item: Training-time costs and numerical stability of Gram-matrix decomposition and whitening are not quantified in the abstract.
paper_title: BISECT: Bilevel Spectral Decomposition for Low-Rank Continual Learning
